questions.question: A page object has `async getError() { return this.error.textContent(); }`. The error appears shortly after the form is submitted. What is the main problem?
options: `textContent()` can't be called inside a class
It reads the text once, so it can return an empty value before the error appears
It throws unless the locator is `private`
It retries for too long and slows the suite
questions.explanation: `textContent()` doesn't wait for the text you expect. Expose the locator and use `await expect(loginPage.error).toHaveText(...)`, which retries.

questions.question: A test reads a `private` locator from a page object. What happens when you run it with `npx playwright test`?
options: The test runs, because Playwright removes types without checking them
Playwright stops with a compile error
The locator is `undefined` at run time
The test is skipped with a warning
questions.explanation: `private` and `readonly` are enforced by the TypeScript compiler only. Run `tsc --noEmit` in CI to catch this kind of misuse.

questions.question: A config sets `trace: 'on-failure'` and a test fails. What do you get?
options: A trace for the failed test
A configuration error before any test runs
A trace for every test
No trace and no warning
questions.explanation: `on-failure` isn't a valid mode, and it's accepted silently. Use `retain-on-failure` to keep traces for failed tests.

questions.question: Where should a test account's cleanup go so it still runs when the test fails?
options: On the last line of the test
Inside the page object's constructor
After `await use(user)` in a fixture
In a `test.step()` at the end of the test
questions.explanation: Code after `use()` is the fixture's teardown, and it runs whether the test passed or failed. Lines at the end of a test are skipped once an assertion fails.

questions.question: A test mocks an API, calls `fetch()` inside `page.evaluate()`, and asserts on the returned JSON. What does it prove?
options: That the page renders the data correctly
Only that the mock returned what the test gave it
That the real API matches the mock
That the app handles server errors
questions.explanation: The app's own code is never exercised, so the test passes even on a page that shows nothing. Let the app make the request and assert on what the user sees.
